title: Sixteen Editions: The Complete History of the Hong Kong 100
claims: The first Hong Kong 100 was held in January 2011 with 175 starters.
The race was founded by Janet Ng and Steve Brammar, two Hong Kong lawyers.
The event is described as the opening round of the World Trail Majors and the largest hundred-kilometre trail race in Asia.
The January 2026 course was shortened by roughly 7 km after Typhoon Wipha damaged the route the previous summer.
The 2026 edition produced the first dead heat for a win, with Veronika Leng and Vietnam's Hà Thị Hậu crossing together in 10:43:35.
The men's course record on the classic route is Qi Min's 9:28:36 in 2018.
The women's course record is Yao Miao's 10:40:52, also set in 2018.
Only three runners have won the hundred twice: Yun Yanqiao in 2013 and 2017, You Peiquan in 2020 and 2023, and Meng Guangfu in 2024 and 2025.
The page notes that the official 2027 GPX is supplied by the organiser and that distances measured from the track may differ slightly from the advertised race distance.
